thread:
elaine: Heads-up, I sketched an alternative for how the cost dashboard should show prefetch/cache credits per-invocation. Current mock lumps them into a single bucket and it confuses product teams.

maya: +1. can you drop the mock? hard to tell where credits are applied.

elaine: pasted a tiny example table:
```
invocation_id | model | raw_tokens | cached_tokens | cache_credit | net_tokens
abc123        | gpt-small | 1200      | 300           | 0.25         | 900
```
The idea: show cached_tokens and the credit multiplier so users see net_tokens.

raj: love the transparency. question: how do we compute cache_credit when a request hits multiple prefetched entries? do we split 50/50 or prorate by token-length?

joel: prorate by token-length seems fair. otherwise weird edgecases where tiny prefetch steals all credit.

maya: UX ask: can we make the per-model breakdown toggleable? some teams just want net cost, not raw tokens.

elaine: yep — default to net_tokens but add a ? tooltip with raw/cached breakdown and a "show raw" toggle.

sandeep: backend nit: our per-invocation telemetry currently only emits total_token_count and cache_hit_tokens aggregated per session. we'll need to change the telemetry proto to include an array of {model, raw, cached} or emit multiple records per-invocation. open to opinions.

devex-bot: CI build for telemetry-schema => failed on proto change in branch feature/token-breakdown (3 tests).

raj: prefer single record per invocation (array) to keep querying simple. downstream dashboards can explode arrays into rows.

joel: arrays in proto are fine but watch cardinality in BigQuery (we explode to repeated fields). storage/cost tradeoff.

maya: also consider quota UX — if we show net_tokens, quotas should be enforced on gross tokens or net? product wants billing to follow net, infra wants quota to follow gross for SLO reasons.

elaine: debate: billing should reflect net cost (customers care about what they pay). Quotas should probably use gross to preserve latency SLOs and avoid denial-of-service via cache manipulation.

raj: agreement: billing = net, quota = gross. need explicit labeling in the console so teams don't get surprised.

sandeep: implementation plan: (1) telemetry proto change to include repeated model token tuples, (2) ingestion pipeline update to compute per-model credits, (3) dashboard join that surfaces both gross/net and caching provenance. I can prototype the proto change but will need an acceptance test for legacy consumers.

maya: can we add a small "why this changed" banner in the rollout? we had a support spike last time when cost columns moved.

elaine: yes — rollout notes + canary flag. plan: behind console feature flag for 2 weeks, then gradual default rollout.

joel: alerting ask: if cache_credit calc changes by >10% for a tenant between releases, auto-open a ticket in #support-cost with a diff, so SRE/product can triage.

elaine: good call. also add an "explain allocation" hover that surfaces which prefetched keys contributed credits (limited to N=5).

raj: small API debate: should we expose an internal-only endpoint that returns per-invocation token-breakdown for debugging? Could be useful for support but dangerous if misused.

sandeep: make it admin-scoped + rate-limited and audit-logged. use the existing internal/observability endpoints pattern.

maya: TL;DR: proto change + dashboard toggle + rollout flag + quota/billing labeling + support alerts + admin debug endpoint.

elaine: I'll file the RFC and include a minimal SQL for the exploder to transform repeated fields. will ping infra for storage impact numbers.

devex-bot: RFC created: RFC-2026-token-breakdown-prefetch-crediting (link: https://rdrwd/notes/RFC-2026).

joel: thanks — can we also add a small unit-econ column per-model that shows cost-per-1k-net-tokens so PMs can compare models directly? even if approximate.

elaine: yep — add to the mock. will include quantization/sku assumptions in RFC.

maya: sounds good, excited. :rocket:

raj: will review the RFC tomorrow.

sandeep: starting proto draft today, will post PR when ready.

elaine: perfect — thanks everyone.
